ordered_diagnoses: Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer

s1.syndrome_frame: Hypertension with multisystem involvement and hemorrhagic stroke
salient_findings: Hepatosplenomegaly with dilated portal and splenic veins
key_facts: Hypertension first noted at age 24 during pregnancy
Hypertension again at age 38 after basal ganglia hemorrhage
Splenomegaly diagnosed at age 21
Younger brother with similar splenomegaly finding
Normochromic microcytic anemia
Thrombocytopenia
Low HDL and elevated triglycerides
Bilateral adrenal lesions with absolute washout 76.5% and relative washout 39%
Hepatosplenomegaly with dilated portal and splenic veins
No symptoms of adrenal hormone excess
Blood pressure controlled on a single antihypertensive agent

shortlist: Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer

shortlist.label: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
shortlist.why_kept: Hypertension, hemorrhagic stroke, and hepatosplenomegaly are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Polycystic kidney disease
shortlist.why_kept: Hypertension and possible renal involvement, although no cysts were mentioned

shortlist.label: Systemic mastocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Splenomegaly, thrombocytopenia, and anemia could be related to mast cell proliferation

shortlist.label: Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Hypertension and possible renal involvement, with a familial component

shortlist.label: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
shortlist.why_kept: Hepatosplenomegaly and possible liver disease, with a familial component

raw.rationale: The combination of basal ganglia hemorrhage, splenomegaly, and hepatosplenomegaly with dilated portal and splenic veins, along with a family history of similar splenomegaly, points towards a vascular disorder. Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) is characterized by arteriovenous malformations that can lead to hemorrhages and is often associated with liver and spleen involvement.

rejected.label: Polycystic kidney disease
rejected.why: There is no mention of kidney cysts or renal dysfunction that would be typical of polycystic kidney disease.

rejected.label: Systemic mastocytosis
rejected.why: The lack of symptoms of mast cell activation, such as flushing, itching, or anaphylaxis, makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer
rejected.why: There is no mention of leiomyomas or renal cell carcinoma, which are hallmarks of this condition.

rejected.label: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
rejected.why: This condition primarily affects the lungs and liver, with no clear connection to the vascular or hemorrhagic findings in this case.
